name: Kegety Gorge
near: The village of Kegeti at the mouth of the gorge (approach via Rot-Front); higher up are the Kegeti dachas (~3.6 km as the crow flies from the catalog point, OSM). ~20 km to Tokmok (too.kg).
elev: From ~1250 m at the mouth to ~3200 m at the river's source (too.kg); Nomad's Land — 1500 m for the lower part. The Kegeti Pass — 3704 m per Pereval.Space (ungraded), 3805 m in other sources (mykg.club) and “about 4000 m” (too.kg).
short: Kegeti is one of the longest (~27 km) gorges of the Kyrgyz Range, ~70 km east of Bishkek: dense Tian Shan spruce forests, a 30 m waterfall, the way to Lake Kol-Tor and a jeep pass into the Kochkor valley.
desc: The Kegeti (Kegety) gorge lies on the northern slope of the Kyrgyz Ala-Too in Chuy district, between the Issyk-Ata and Shamsi gorges, 70 km east of Bishkek and 20 km from Tokmok. It is about 27 km long, with elevations from 1250 m to 3200 m at the source (too.kg). The densest Schrenk spruce forests in the Chuy Valley are here. In the lower part is the Kegeti waterfall, about 30 m high; in the right tributary is the turquoise Lake Kol-Tor (in summer 2026 the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) drained water from it with siphons because of the threat of overflow). In the upper reaches the road goes to the Kegeti Pass (3704 m per Pereval.Space) — a crossing to the East Karakol valley and Kochkor, popular with jeepers and cycle tourists. Tourist infrastructure is minimal: yurts and guesthouses by the first waterfall and in the Kol-Tor tract.
guide: Kegeti is a gorge for those who want spruce forests and open space without the crowds of Ala-Archa. For an easy day the Kegeti waterfall (30 m, 5 minutes from the road) is enough, and if you have the energy, turn onto the trail to Lake Kol-Tor: 14 km round trip and turquoise water surrounded by spruces. Keep away from the edge of the road above the river: in summer 2026 a car with children fell into the river here. For experienced jeepers there is the road over the Kegeti Pass (about 3700 m) into the Kochkor valley, but only in a prepared 4×4. Bring your own water — do not drink from the river because of livestock.
see: The Kegeti waterfall (~30 m) in the lower part of the gorge; Lake Kol-Tor in the right tributary; dense Schrenk spruce forests; the mountain Kegeti River; the road to the Kegeti Pass (3704 m) with views of the main range.
skip: You have an ordinary car and aren't ready for a bumpy dirt road — after ~10 km of asphalt the road gets worse. You have already been to the Kegeti waterfall and Kol-Tor (separate entries) — the gorge itself without a trek adds little. You are looking for services: there is almost no infrastructure.
diff: The waterfall — easy (≈200 m and 5 minutes from the road, hiking.kg). Lake Kol-Tor — moderate: ~14 km round trip, several hours (TripAdvisor). The Kegeti Pass — ungraded on foot (Pereval.Space), but by vehicle only a prepared 4×4 and an experienced driver (too.kg).
when: June — September for hikes to Kol-Tor and driving the upper road; the waterfall is accessible from spring to autumn. The trails are slippery in rain (TripAdvisor). The Kegeti Pass — only at the height of summer; in winter the upper part is covered with snow (based on the general mountain regime, not confirmed).
hours: The gorge is open 24 hours. At the entrance there is a checkpoint/barrier with an eco fee (2024). There is no fixed operating schedule; guesthouses and yurts operate mostly in summer.
daytime: Morning: the drive and the trail to Kol-Tor take the whole day, and the light on the lake is better before noon; leave Bishkek by 7–8 a.m. At the waterfall — midday, when the sun is in the gorge (editorial).
how: From Bishkek east via Krasnaya Rechka, Yuryevka, Syn-Tash and Rot-Front to the village of Kegeti, then up the gorge (85 km / 2 h 15 min to the waterfall — hiking.kg). Paved for ~10 km in the gorge, then dirt (too.kg). The turn to Kol-Tor and the parking area are a separate route.
needcar: Yes: a car, taxi or tour. Public transport does not go into the gorge itself (too.kg); the marshrutka (minibus) goes only to the village of Kegeti.
self: Yes, by car (preferably with high ground clearance): the waterfall is next to the road, and the trail to Kol-Tor is popular. Over the pass — only with experience and a prepared vehicle.
roadtype: Paved for ~10 km from the village into the gorge, then a rocky dirt road (“very bumpy at the end” — TripAdvisor); the upper section and the Kegeti Pass — only a prepared 4×4 (too.kg).
traveltime: Bishkek → Kegeti waterfall: 85 km, 2 h 15 min (hiking.kg); TripAdvisor — ~2 h. The hike to Kol-Tor — ~14 km round trip, 5–7 h.
stay: Yurts with meals opposite the first waterfall; a small hotel beyond the first barrier; a guesthouse in the Kol-Tor tract (too.kg); Kegety Tour guesthouse — 1500 som/person with three meals a day (asia-hikes, per group 6 data). A few tent spots between the first and second waterfalls.
net: There is a signal only in the lower part of the gorge up to the first waterfall, higher up it is unstable (too.kg). The operator is not specified.
entry: Eco fee of about 200 som per passenger car at the Kegeti checkpoint (hiking.kg, 2024). The current 2026 tariff is not confirmed.
transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) to the village of Kegeti — 50 som (2024, not confirmed); tours $70–370 (TripAdvisor). The price of a taxi Bishkek — Kegeti was not found.
bring: A supply of drinking water (springs are few, and river water must not be drunk because of livestock — too.kg), trekking shoes (slippery after rain), a rain jacket, a snack, cash for the eco fee and yurts, an offline map (the signal disappears after the waterfall).
warn: A narrow road above the river: on 23.06.2026 a car's brakes failed and it fell into the river — two children died (Kaktus.media, Vesti.kg). Drive slowly, in a roadworthy car. Lake Kol-Tor was under threat of overflow in August 2026 — the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) installed 204 m siphons (Gazeta.kg 12.08.2026); watch for mudflow warnings. The upper road — 4×4 only. Do not drink river water.
food: Lunch in the yurts by the first waterfall (Kyrgyz cuisine, kumis in summer — per too.kg the yurts feed guests); at the Kol-Tor guesthouse — full board. Specific menus and prices are not confirmed.
reviews: TripAdvisor “Kegety Gorge”: 4.6/5, 10 reviews (07.10.2026); Google Maps — no unambiguous listing for the gorge (the Kegeti waterfall — 4.7/5, 682 ratings as of 03.10.2026, group 6). Pros: a picturesque gorge with spruce forests, fewer people, the waterfall and Kol-Tor. Cons: a bumpy road at the end, high clearance needed, few services.
p.sum: Kegety is 85 km and about 2 h 15 min east of Bishkek; drive via Rot-Front to the village of Kegeti. The first ~10 km in the gorge are paved, then a bumpy dirt road, so a car with high ground clearance, a taxi or a weekend group tour (from 690–900 som, 2025) is best. Marshrutka (minibus) No. 303 from the East Bus Station only goes to the village. The main goals are the waterfall, 5 minutes from the road, and the turquoise Lake Kol-Tor (2725 m): 7.5 km and +900 m one way, 4–7 h round trip. You can overnight at the Kegety Tour guesthouses (≈1500 som with meals) or Sun City (Ak-Sai). Drive carefully: in June 2026 a car fell into the river from the narrow road above it.

p.iti.2.title: What to combine
p.iti.2.plan: The Burana Tower (Tokmok), Issyk-Ata (≈1 h west), the Kegeti waterfall (the same trip), the Boom Gorge and Chon-Kemin further east
p.season: May — June: full waterfalls, mud on the road after rain. July — September: the best time for Kol-Tor, crowded on weekends. August 2026: the Ministry of Emergency Situations (MChS) was lowering the level of Kol-Tor because of the threat of a breakout — watch for warnings. October: golden autumn, cold at the lake. November — April: the top of the gorge is under snow, guesthouses are closed
p.budget.economy: ≈1000–2500 som: a weekend group tour 690–900 som (2025) or marshrutka (minibus) ≈100 som + hitchhiking; eco fee (≈200 som per car), lunch in a yurt
p.budget.comfort: A private tour €280 per group (Tripster) or $190–215/person (Expedia); a night in a guesthouse ≈1500 som with meals
p.permits: No permit needed. At the gorge entrance there is a checkpoint/barrier with an eco fee of ≈200 som per passenger car (hiking.kg, 2024); the 2026 tariff is not confirmed
p.access: The waterfall — for everyone, including children and older people (5 minutes from the road, but the road is bumpy). Kol-Tor — only for the fit; Tripster: not suitable for children. Stroller — only at the yurts. Dogs — possible, but there are shepherd dogs on the pastures
